title: The pawn
outcomes: Moves a pawn one square forward, or two from its starting row, to reach a target
Captures one square diagonally forward and knows a piece straight ahead blocks a pawn
Says in one sentence how a pawn's walk and its capture differ

steps.title: Grab the star
steps.say: Move the pawn forward onto the star.

steps.text: A **pawn** moves straight forward, one square at a time, never backward. From its starting row it may move two squares in one go. These are White's pawns; Black's walk down the board the other way. Promotion and en passant come in later lessons.
A pawn **captures** differently: one square **diagonally forward**, onto an enemy piece. The enemy piece stands on a star in the next boards.
A pawn **cannot capture straight ahead**. A piece directly in front blocks it, and the pawn cannot walk around it. This includes the two-square first move: both squares ahead must be empty.

steps.caption: A knight stands straight ahead of the pawn. The pawn cannot move at all.
Same block, but now a rook stands on the forward diagonal. The pawn can take it.
The pawn is on its starting row, but a piece stands on the square just ahead. The two-square move is blocked too.

steps.prompt: Say it back in three short parts: one fact about walking, one about capturing, one about blocking. Then compare with the model answer.

steps.text: **Model answer.** A pawn walks straight forward, two squares from its starting row, but captures one square diagonally forward. A piece straight ahead blocks it.

steps.prompt: Pick one legal pawn move on a board you have not seen and say how you know. Then: not yet, mostly, or ready?
